title: Silvergate - VPC connectivity & private endpoint eval
next_steps: Redwood: share private endpoints doc + VPC peering checklist (by 2025-12-05)
Customer: provide list of subnets & peerable IP ranges (by 2025-12-08)
Schedule technical POC/baseline test next week (propose 2025-12-10)
action_items: Maya Chen - send VPC peering diagram and ingress/egress table - due 2025-12-05
Diego Alvarez - prepare POC proposal with target latency metrics and test plan - due 2025-12-07
Raj Patel - export current VPC CIDR blocks and NAT/egress gateway config - due 2025-12-08
Lena Ortiz - confirm KMS/bring-your-own-key requirements and compliance checklist - due 2025-12-09
meeting_summary: Discovery call to understand Silvergate's network/topology constraints for a Redwood Private deployment. Main topics: VPC peering vs private endpoints, region residency, egress controls, KMS/BYOK, and timeline for a POC. Action items and next steps agreed; plan to exchange diagrams and schedule POC baseline test.
transcript:
00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side. Quick roll call?
00:08 - Raj Patel: Raj here.
00:10 - Lena Ortiz: Lena.
00:11 - Tommy Wu: Tommy.
00:12 - Aisha Khan: Aisha.
00:15 - Maya Chen: Great. Diego and Priya from SE are with me, they'll handle the deep network bits. We scheduled 50 minutes so we'll focus on your architecture and constraints, then next steps.
00:28 - Diego Alvarez: Hi, quick agenda: intakes - what you run today, connectivity options (peering v private endpoints), compliance and KMS needs, then POC scope.
00:40 - Raj Patel: We currently run on GCP us-east4, have a pretty strict egress policy - all external calls must go through our egress nat gateway or managed proxies. No public IPs allowed on compute.
00:52 - Tommy Wu: Also multi-account org, we prefer cross-project peering or VPC peering, and transit via our firewall stack.
01:05 - Maya Chen: Understood. Redwood Private can run in a customer VPC via our private deployment model or we can peer to your VPC from a vendor VPC. Prio question: do you want the control plane in your VPC or can it remain in Redwood-managed infra?
01:22 - Raj Patel: For this use case we need the control plane to be private in our VPC - we can't have control plane traffic traversing public internet.
01:31 - Lena Ortiz: Correct. Also encryption at rest - we need BYOK with KMS integration and audit trails for model requests.
01:40 - Priya Nair: That's doable, we have customers who rotate keys via KMS. A few notes: we support native cloud KMS integrations and HSM via partners; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
01:55 - Aisha Khan: Do you support regional lock? Our data residency rules require inference to run in eu-west1 exclusively for some customers.
02:05 - Maya Chen: Yes, we can pin deployments to regions. For this call, you said us-east4 - are you evaluating multi-region or single region?
02:15 - Raj Patel: Initially single region but planning to expand. The big concern is egress — if you run in a vendor VPC and we peer, can we force traffic out to our egress appliances?
02:28 - Diego Alvarez: Short answer: yes. With VPC peering we can route subnets so that outbound to the internet flows via your route table -> nat gateway. However, cross-project peering requires you to advertise the right routes and ensure no overlapping CIDRs.
02:40 - Tommy Wu: Right, overlapping was our previous headache. We won't have overlapping. Another concern is private endpoints - we'd prefer private endpoints to avoid peering if possible, less operational load.
02:53 - Maya Chen: We offer Private Endpoint support (our side exposes a private ALB/NLB in the same region and you create an endpoint and DNS entry). That avoids full VPC peering. Tradeoffs: peering gives lower latency and a flat network path; private endpoints are simpler but can add cross-zone hops depending on topology.
03:10 - Raj Patel: Do private endpoints support model streaming (server-sent events / chunked responses)? We rely on streaming responses for our real-time product.
03:21 - Priya Nair: Streaming over private endpoints works. We've seen a small increase in tail latency in some cross-zone setups, but for most workloads it's within SLA. If you need consistent sub-50ms token latencies we'd recommend peering + colocated instances.
03:38 - Lena Ortiz: About audit logs and retention: we need 13 months, and logs must be immutable. Can we pull logs to our GCS or Splunk?
03:49 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, Redwood can forward logs via push mechanism to your GCS bucket or to a logging endpoint. For immutability, we can support append-only config and demonstrate retention controls. We'll include concrete docs.
04:05 - Aisha Khan: On KMS: do you allow us to hold keys entirely? BYOK? Or do you need to manage a portion of keys?
04:14 - Maya Chen: We support BYOK where Redwood never has the plaintext key; the runtime integrates with your KMS to decrypt model artifacts or disk keys at boot. Some customers use HSM-backed keys via partner integrations. We'll share the integration matrix.
04:30 - Raj Patel: Networking specifics: if we do peering, what's the IP space requirement on your side? We need to ensure routing tables fit into our existing peering.
04:40 - Priya Nair: Typical pattern is to allocate a /20 or /21 block for the Redwood-managed VPC that will host the inference pool. We can go as small as /24 per subnet but for scale and high availability we recommend larger blocks.
04:55 - Tommy Wu: Could we do egress hairpinning? e.g., traffic from Redwood back to our services should come back through our firewall so the ACLs apply.
05:05 - Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can set route priorities so traffic destined to your IP space returns via peering and then out of your egress chain. We usually add explicit route table entries to avoid asymmetric paths.
05:20 - Raj Patel: Anything about DNS? We use internal DNS zones and split-horizon. How will name resolution work with private endpoints?
05:30 - Priya Nair: For private endpoints we give you a private DNS name that you can override in your internal zone, or we can provide the IPs and you point A records. With peering, standard internal DNS forwarding works if you allow lookups. Some customers use conditional forwarders.
05:48 - Lena Ortiz: Security review: do you have SOC2 type II? Any penetration test reports?
05:55 - Maya Chen: Yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 docs; we also publish a pen test summary. We'll send the links. For customers with extra compliance we support penetration testing windows and can sign an NDA for specific findings.
06:12 - Aisha Khan: Latency question again: what's the typical p50/p95 for token generation when colocated vs peered vs private endpoint?
06:21 - Diego Alvarez: Colocated within the same VPC model: p50 can be <20ms per token for smaller models under concurrency; peering is similar, p95 might be 50-80ms depending on sequence length; private endpoints add a small delta, so p95 often sits 80-140ms in our experience. We'll attach benchmarks.
06:42 - Raj Patel: For the POC we want to validate latency and cost per 1M tokens; can you run a baseline with our prompts?
06:50 - Maya Chen: Yes, Diego will propose a test harness — you'll share a representative prompt set and we'll run tests in your environment or closest region. Expected timeline to run: 3-5 days once we have network access.
07:05 - Tommy Wu: On certificate management for private endpoints, who rotates certs?
07:12 - Priya Nair: If you host the endpoint in your VPC then you control certs; if it's a Redwood-managed private endpoint we manage certs and rotate them, but we support mutual TLS if you require client certs.
07:26 - Lena Ortiz: Does Redwood support SAML SSO for Console access? We need RBAC and SCIM for provisioning.
07:34 - Maya Chen: Yes SAML SSO and SCIM are supported; RBAC with roles that map to your groups. We'll include the SAML metadata file and a sample role mapping.
07:44 - Aisha Khan: Any dependencies on specific cloud provider primitives? We're mostly GCP but have a subset on AWS.
07:51 - Diego Alvarez: Redwood runtime supports GCP, AWS and Azure; for private deployments we have provider-specific docs. Keep in mind NAT gateway behavior and network ACLs are provider specific.
08:05 - Raj Patel: Regarding patching and upgrades in private: how are model updates handled? We need canary rollouts and version pinning.
08:14 - Priya Nair: You can pin model versions in the deployment manifest. For upgrades we do canary rollouts with traffic split and automatic rollback if latency/quality regressions are detected. All of that can be orchestrated from your control plane.
08:29 - Tommy Wu: Do you support runtime telemetry to our tracing system? We use Jaeger and Datadog traces.
08:35 - Diego Alvarez: Yes we emit traces and can push spans to your tracing collectors or forward via OTLP.
08:42 - Raj Patel: Time for the constraints recap: we require private control plane in our VPC, BYOK via GCP KMS, audit log forwarding to GCS, single-region us-east4 initially, strict egress through our NAT/proxies, and we prefer peering for latency but will consider private endpoints for simpler ops. Is that right?
09:01 - Maya Chen: Correct. Anything else?
09:04 - Lena Ortiz: SLA expectations: we want to understand recovery time and support response SLAs for P0. Do you have dedicated support tiers for Private?
09:12 - Maya Chen: Yes Dedicated/Private comes with enterprise SLAs and a named CSM/devops escalation path. We'll attach the SLA PDF.
09:21 - Aisha Khan: Quick question on data residency: if we expand to EU, will we need separate peering/federation?
09:28 - Diego Alvarez: Yes usually you provision separate private deployments in the target region and either peer them or use cross-region private link; we can help design a multi-region architecture.
09:39 - Maya Chen: Next steps recap: we'll send the VPC peering checklist, private endpoints how-to, SOC2 and KMS integration docs. Diego will draft a POC plan and propose dates. Raj and Lena will share CIDRs and KMS requirements.
09:55 - Raj Patel: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? Not that I see. We'll review docs and pick a POC window.
10:03 - Tommy Wu: One last nit: do you have recommended MTU settings? Our infra had issues with jumbo frames once.
10:10 - Priya Nair: Standard MTU 1500 is recommended; we can support jumbo frames in some setups but it's extra config. We'll note that in the checklist.
10:22 - Aisha Khan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
10:24 - Maya Chen: Thanks. We'll follow up with the action items.
10:28 - (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cash, Tran-sit phrasing) and some speaker overlaps. Shared artifacts referenced: "Redwood private endpoints doc" (link to be sent), "SOC2 package" (link), "POC test harness proposal (Diego)".
